properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for the Goulburn River Seymour to Shepparton including Mooroopna and Kialla.

This Advice replaces the message issued at 4:23pm Wednesday. 

The Goulburn River at Shepparton is currently peaking around 10.05 metres. The Goulburn River may remain above the minor flood level (9.50metres) until Friday morning. 

The Broken River at Orrvale peaked Wednesday afternoon around 7.72 metres with moderate flooding, and a separate message has been issued. 

The Seven Creeks at Kialla West peaked around midday Wednesday with moderate flooding. and a separate message has been issued . 
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.
  • Farmers should consider moving livestock and machinery to higher ground.
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Contact family members and neighbours to ensure they are aware of the situation.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings.
To check if your property is prone to flooding, 
  • Check the Goulburn Broken Catchment Management Authority's Community Flood Information Portal and download your property information statement at: https://my.floodreport.com.au/gbcma/
  • For full instructions, and more local flood information, download the Shepparton, Mooroopna & Kialla Local Flood Guide at: www.ses.vic.gov.au/plan-and-stay-safe/flood-guides/greater-shepparton-city-council
  • Try the new Greater Shepparton Emergency Dashboard https://emergency.greatershepparton.com.au/ to view local emergency information.
Impacts in the Shepparton, Mooroopna and Kialla areas:
  • The Ross Edwards Causeway is not expected to close.
  • Riverside areas and flats will be flooded for several days, including camps, areas near the Shepparton Lawn tennis court and Princess Park near the Bocce club and behind Aquamoves.  
  • High river levels and potential flooding of farmland and parks close to the rivers and creeks.
  • Watt Road closed both directions between Riverview Drive and McLennan Street. 
  • Riverview Drive closed both directions between Botanic Gardens Avenue and Watt Road.
  • Raftery Road closed both directions between Edgewater Road, Kialla and Seven Creeks Drive.
  • All vehicle & walking tracks within the Arcadia Streamside Reserve, Shepparton Regional Park & Gemmills Swamp Wildlife Reserve were closed on Monday. 
  • Floodwater may cover South Quinnan Parade and Hassett Street near Lincoln Drive.
  • In Shepparton, Stewart Reserve, the fenced dog park, Jaycee Park and the Swans Football/Netball club may be impacted by floodwater. 
  • There is floodwater in Jordan Place, Shepparton near The Boulevard. 

Due to the Broken River flooding, farmland and yards around Doyles Road, parts of Kialla Lakes Drive and Gordon Drive, and many streets in Kialla Lakes are likely to be covered by floodwater. 

Impacts at Toolamba:
  • Tracks in the forested areas west of Goulburn River, such as Steves Track will be flooded.

Road Closures
  • Other local roads may be closed and low bridges may be underwater.
  • For the latest road closures go to: traffic.transport.vic.gov.au
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 14/08/2026 12:10 pm or as the situation changes.

Use multiple sources to stay informed:
  • www.emergency.vic.gov.au
  • VicEmergency Hotline - freecall 1800 226 226
  • VicEmergency app
  • Facebook
  • Tune in to ABC Local Radio, commercial and designated community radio stations, or News24 TV.
For health information and support contact the below organisations: 
Lifeline on www.lifeline.org.au or phone 13 11 14. 
Beyond Blue on www.beyondblue.org.au or phone 1300 224 636. 
Kids Helpine on www.kidshelp.com.au or phone 1800 551 800. 
SANE Australia on www.sane.org or phone 1800 187 263.

Accessibility: 
The following services can help you, or someone you know, access information during an emergency. 
  • To access this information in other languages, call the Translating and Interpreting Service on 131 450 (freecall) and ask them to call VicEmergency Hotline. 
  • If you are deaf, hard of hearing, or have a speech/communication impairment, contact the National Relay Service and ask them to call the VicEmergency Hotline.

This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for the King River.

Moderate flooding is estimated to be occurring along the King River at the Docker Road Bridge, and falling slowly. The King River at Docker Rd Bridge may fall below the Moderate flood level (3.95 metres) Thursday afternoon. 

The King River at Lake William Hovell (Downstream) fell below the minor flood level (1.80 metres) yesterday afternoon. 

The Ovens River in Wangaratta peaked at 12.65 metres on Tuesday afternoon. The highest part of the Ovens river flood is now downstream of Wangaratta and approaching Peechelba East. 
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do:

properties.webBody:
This Minor Flood Warning is being issued for parts of the Goulburn River downstream of Shepparton. 

Minor flooding is possible at McCoys bridge from Saturday. 

Significant rainfall across the Goulburn River catchment on Sunday resulted in river level rises and areas of minor to moderate flooding at Shepparton, Mooroopna and Kialla along the Goulburn and Broken Rivers and the Seven Creeks.

The Goulburn River at McCoys Bridge is currently at 6.91 metres and rising, below the minor flood level. 

The Goulburn River at McCoys Bridge may reach around the minor flood level (9.00 metres) during Saturday.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and remain alert.
What you should do: 
  • People living or camping on the Goulburn River between Shepparton and Kanyapella should expect river level rises on Friday and Saturday as floodwater arrives from Shepparton. 
  • Farmers should consider moving livestock and machinery from along the river to higher ground. 
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Monitor river levels. Go to www.bom.gov.au/vic/warnings/
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings.
Impacts in your area: 
  • High river levels and potential flooding in areas close to rivers and streams.

This Moderate Flood Warning is being issued for the Loddon River-Loddon Weir to Kerang.

  • Rainfall observed across the Loddon catchment over the weekend has resulted in river level rises across the catchment.
  • At 11.00am, August 13 the Loddon River at Loddon Weir was at 6.23m, above the moderate flood level (6.0m).
  • The Loddon River at Appin South is currently at 0.63m and rising and may exceed the minor flood level (2.80 m) during Friday.
  • Further rises are possible as upstream flows arrive.
Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and be prepared to act if your situation changes.
What you should do: 
  • Be prepared to act if your situation changes.
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwaters
  • Farmers should consider moving livestock and machinery to higher ground.
  • Stay informed by listening to emergency broadcasters and monitoring warnings.
Impacts in your area: 
  • High river levels and potential flooding in areas close to rivers and streams.
  • Over-floor flooding of dwellings is not currently expected. 
  • Impacts expected to be limited to inundation of lower areas of Loddon floodplain with possible inundation of some minor local roads.
  • Roads and bridges may be closed due to flooding.
  • Boating in floodwaters is dangerous due to debris, submerged trees and other hidden dangers.

properties.location: Avoca River downstream of Charlton Town
properties.webBody:
This Moderate Flood Warning is being issued for Avoca River downstream of Charlton Town.

  • Moderate rainfall was recorded across the Avoca River catchment during Sunday and into Monday, with the heaviest falls recorded in the upper parts of the catchment. 
  • The Avoca River downstream of Charlton Town is at 5.95m and rising, above the moderate flood level (5.0m).
  • The Avoca River downstream from Charlton Town is expected to peak tonight into tomorrow morning.
Stay safe - avoid the flooded area. Be aware of potential hazards caused by flooding and never enter floodwater.
What you should do:
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never enter floodwater.
  • Farmers should move livestock and machinery to higher ground.
If you choose to leave:
  • Remember to take your pets, mobile phone, spare clothes and medications.
  • Travel to the home of family or friends who are in a safe location, away from flooding.
  • Turn off gas and electricity at your home or workplace.
  • Be aware of any road closures when you leave.
If you are travelling:
  • Do not enter flooded areas. Turn around a find a safe alternative route.
  • Be aware of road hazards including mud, debris and damaged roads or bridges.
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.
If you stay or if it is unsafe to leave:
  • Make sure you have enough food, drinking water, medications and pet food to survive for three to five days in case you become isolated.
  • Use plugs, sandbags or household items to block toilets, sinks and drains to stop sewerage backflow.
  • Lift it - move valuables and vital household items up on high surfaces, such as on top of tables, chairs, benches and beds.
Impacts in your area:
  • Downstream of Charlton, in the Glenloth, Bunguluke and Ninyeunook areas, floodwaters are expected to arrive later and may persist for several days as they move through the floodplain.
  • Floodwater may spread across farmland and affect local roads.
  • The Boort-Wycheproof Road crossing at the Avoca River may become flooded and unsafe to use.
  • There is currently no impacts expected for the Quambatook township.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 14/08/2026 03:30 pm or as the situation changes.

properties.location: Avoca River to Charlton Town
properties.webBody:
This Moderate Flood Warning is being issued for Avoca River to Charlton Town.

  • Moderate rainfall was recorded across the Avoca River catchment during Sunday and into Monday, with the heaviest falls recorded in the upper parts of the catchment. River level rises are occurring along the Avoca River.
  • Minor flooding is occurring at Yawong Weir. 
  • Moderate flooding is occurring at Charlton Downstream and is likely at Charlton Town. 
  • The Avoca River at Charlton Town is currently at 5.79 m and rising, with minor flooding. 
  • The Avoca River at Charlton Town is likely to exceed the moderate flood level (5.90 m) from Thursday afternoon. 
  • The river may peak near 6.70 m overnight Thursday into Friday, with moderate flooding. 
  • The river may remain above the moderate flood level (5.90m) until Friday afternoon.
Prepare for flooding now. Take actions to protect your life and property against potential hazards caused by flooding.
What you should do:
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never enter floodwater.
  • Farmers should move livestock and machinery to higher ground.
  • If you are camping close to a creek or river, you may be at risk of flooding and need to move to higher ground, away from waterways.
  • Rising floodwater can be dangerous. Be aware of water levels rising near you.
If you choose to leave:
  • Remember to take your pets, mobile phone, spare clothes and medications.
  • Travel to the home of family or friends who are in a safe location, away from flooding.
  • Turn off gas and electricity at your home or workplace.
  • Be aware of any road closures when you leave.
If you are travelling:
  • Do not enter flooded areas. Turn around a find a safe alternative route.
  • Be aware of road hazards including mud, debris and damaged roads or bridges.
  • Floodwater is dangerous - never drive, walk or ride through floodwater.
If you stay or if it is unsafe to leave:
  • Make sure you have enough food, drinking water, medications and pet food to survive for three to five days in case you become isolated.
  • Use plugs, sandbags or household items to block toilets, sinks and drains to stop sewerage backflow.
  • Lift it - move valuables and vital household items up on high surfaces, such as on top of tables, chairs, benches and beds.
Impacts in your area:
  • Floodwater may affect Gordon Park Caravan Park, with conditions similar to the December 2023 Boxing Day flood.
  • Over-floor flooding of homes is not currently expected.
  • The Boort-Wycheproof Road crossing at the Avoca River may become flooded and unsafe to use.
  • Flooding of farmland downstream of Glenloth around Bunguluke and Ninyeunook, and inundation of local roads such as Jeruk River Road North and Ninyeunook Road, is possible.
  • Floodwaters may persist for several days as they move through the floodplain.
This message was issued by State Emergency Service.

The next update is expected by 14/08/2026 03:30 pm or as the situation changes.

Use multiple sources to stay informed:
  • www.emergency.vic.gov.au
  • VicEmergency Hotline - freecall 1800 226 226

This is a Final Minor Flood Warning for Loddon River Laanecoorie to Loddon Weir.

  • Along the Loddon River at Laanecoorie Reservoir the river level has fallen below the minor flood level.
  • The Loddon River at Laanecoorie Reservoir is currently at 1.35 m and steady, below the minor flood level and is expected to remain below the minor flood level (1.50 m).
The threat of flooding is reduced. Stay informed - monitor your local conditions and beware of hazards remaining in the warning area.
What you should do:
  • Drive slowly, obey all roadblocks and never drive through floodwaters.
  • If cleaning after damage has occurred, protect your health and safety. Wear strong boots, gloves and protective clothing and wash your hands and clothes regularly.
Impacts in your area: 
  • Damage to roads and buildings caused by flooding may still exist in your area. 
  • Check the VicTraffic website (www.traffic.transport.vic.gov.au) for road closures and follow instructions from emergency services.
